I am an old man now, and this small piece of land near the house is where I plant my yam. The soil here I have worked for many years, so I put the droppings from my goats and some household ash on it before planting — that is what keeps it giving. Fertilizer from the government does not always reach us, and for yam the manure works better anyway. I use the seed yams I kept from last harvest, like my father taught me, and my sons help me make the mounds because my back is not what it was.
